correctness.rationale: PASS. The unit-cost full committee with k elected candidates, n approval voters and at least one supporter per elected candidate is tested using the literal weak EJR+ up-to-one criterion n(u_i+1)>k|T| for at least one i in T subset of challengers supporters, and strong payment criterion F_i(S,x)=1_{i in Ax}/t +sum_{d in W}1_{i in A_d}/max(t,|S intersect A_d|)>k/n for some i in S, t=|S intersect Ax|>0. Verified analytically the bound F_i>=1/t+u_i/n gives no separation for k<=2; for n<=2, the complete S={1,2} payment sum is k+1, using all winners supported; for n=k=3, weak requires u_i>=t, giving F_i>=1/t+t/3>1. Therefore n+m>=8, and (n,k,m)=(3,4,5) or (4,3,4) are the only boundary regimes. Independently reconstructed exhaustive exact Fraction comparison of every elected multiset and challenger mask: 1470 and 10200 cases, respectively; exactly 18/6 separating labelled signatures, respectively 4/1 voter-permutation orbits, and 2 Pareto-efficient orbits total. The two explicit Pareto witnesses have strong scores exactly k/n, thus violate the strict > condition; proper-subset approver criterion proves efficiency for k-of-(k+1). Full finite census, unlike sampling, covers the specified boundary.
